facts.text: Foggy Bottom earned its name from the misty fog that rolled over its swampy southern banks and the industrial smog of early factories.
During the Civil War, Union troops established Camp Fry on 23rd Street south of Washington Circle, a training base for the Veteran Reserve Corps.
Christian Heurich Brewing Company, founded by German immigrant Christian Heurich in 1872, became a regional powerhouse and major employer in Foggy Bottom.
Foggy Bottom’s decline began in the early 20th century as the C&O Canal fell out of use and Prohibition cut brewery traffic, pushing residents northward.
Founded in 1955, the Foggy Bottom Association still hosts block parties and walking tours that celebrate the neighborhood’s historic character.
Rock Creek snakes between Foggy Bottom and Georgetown, meeting the Potomac in Foggy Bottom’s northeast near Virginia Avenue.
